_comment: Mutants that survive because no test could observe them, not because a test is missing.
Every entry needs a reason someone can check. Writing one is the point: it forces the
question 'is this genuinely unobservable, or have I just not thought of the case?' —
which is how two real gaps in syncStatus.ts were found rather than allowlisted.
Matched on file + rule + the trimmed source line, so an entry stops applying when the
line it justifies is edited. That is deliberate: the justification should be re-read.

equivalent.reason: Boundary-only, and both branches agree at the boundary. When the remainder is exactly MIN_READER_WIDTH the early return gives the reader exactly that; falling through instead computes a listGive of 0 and reaches the same widths. Verified by exhaustive search over containerWidth 1..3000 against every combination of the preferred widths and the three sidebar preferences (~500k inputs): no input distinguishes it.

Same boundary, one branch later: at exact equality the sidebarGive computed below is 0, so the fall-through returns the widths the early return would have. Same exhaustive search, no distinguishing input.

The guard and the function's last line cover the same case twice. It differs from `<` only when the path is exactly the delimiter plus the name ('/Receipts'), and there the slice produces '' — which the trailing `|| undefined` turns into undefined anyway. Checked against every combination of four names and eight prefixes: no input distinguishes them. The guard is kept for the comment above it, which explains a real off-by-one that predates it.

The sRGB linearisation knee. It differs from `<` only at s exactly 0.03928, which is channel 10.0164 — and every channel here comes from an integer 0-255 divided by 255, so that value cannot occur. Unreachable rather than untested.

Differs from `<` only when the alpha is exactly 25, and a four-digit hex doubles a single nibble — so its alpha can only be 0, 17, 34, 51 … 255. 25 is not among them. The eight-digit form CAN be exactly 25 ('#ffffff19') and that boundary is tested.

The guard is an early return, not the only defence. Turning any of its `||` into `&&` makes it never fire, and the value then falls through to the rgb() and hex parsers — neither of which matches 'transparent', 'inherit', 'initial', 'currentcolor' or an empty string, so the function returns null anyway. Verified by running those five values against both regexes. The guard is kept because it states the intent; four separate mutations of it are the same fact reported four times.

For a string the two halves say the same thing: '' is falsy and has length 0, and every other string is truthy with length > 0. `firstToken` only ever produces a string, and the only falsy one it can produce is '' (from a blank input). Checked against '', ' ', 'a', 'abc', '0' and a Message-ID: no value distinguishes && from ||. The length check is belt-and-braces, not logic.

Redundant second lock. `getSyncCutoffTimestamp` on the next line returns null for anything <= 0 and the null is checked, so a syncDays of 0 returns 0 either way. The guard is here because the consequence of it being wrong is deleting the account's entire mail — worth two locks even when only one can be observed.

`&&` binds tighter than `||`, so the mutant reads `email || (displayName && 'Orbit Mail')` and the first arm still wins. `accounts.email` is NOT NULL and an account cannot be created without one (saveAccount keys on the address), so the later arms are unreachable — they are there for a row corrupted by hand. The other `||` on this line is caught.

Both arms reach the same result by a different route. Falling through with a null likePattern builds a query whose LIKE parameters are null, which matches nothing; falling through with an empty accountId scopes to `account_id = ''`, which no row has. The early return is a shortcut, not the thing that makes the answer right — asserted from the outside, the two are indistinguishable.
Same shape: falling through queries `account_id = '' AND message_id = ?` (or the reverse), and no row matches an empty column value. The guard saves a query, not a wrong answer.

`''` and `null` are both falsy, and every caller of canonicalizeMessageId tests the result for truthiness (`if (own)`, `if (!own) continue`) rather than comparing it to null. Returning the empty string instead of null changes the value and not one decision made with it.

The branch body is `for (let i = 1; i < refs.length; i++)`, which does nothing when refs is empty. Entering it for a message with no references is a no-op, so the guard saves an iteration rather than a wrong grouping.

Spreading an empty array yields the same contents, so both branches return the same rows in the same order when there are no drafts. The conditional exists to avoid copying the summaries array on every read of every non-Drafts folder, which is a cost and not a behaviour.

recalculateFolderUnread recomputes the count from the rows, so running it when nothing changed writes back the value already there. The guard avoids a folder-sized COUNT on every poll that finds no flag changes — which is most of them — and nothing downstream can tell the difference.

equivalent.code: if (!cur || r.date < cur.date || (r.date === cur.date && own < cur.id)) {
equivalent.reason: The mutated `<` is the tie-break `own <= cur.id`, reached only when the dates are equal. `own === cur.id` means this row *is* the current representative, so replacing it with itself stores the same value. The date comparison on the same line — the one that decides which message roots a thread — is caught.

equivalent.code: const from = PROVIDER_LABELS[existing.provider as Provider] ?? existing.provider
equivalent.reason: PROVIDER_LABELS maps every Provider to a non-empty display string, so the looked-up value is never falsy-but-present. The fallback only fires for a provider value not in the union, where the key is missing and `??` and `||` agree.
Same table, same argument: every entry is a non-empty string, so the two operators can only differ on a key that is absent, where both take the fallback.

setAccountSignature stores `signature.trim() || null`, so the column is either null or a non-empty string — the empty string is never written. The suite asserts exactly that (a whitespace-only signature reads back as ''), which is what makes this equivalence checkable rather than assumed.
FlagColor is a union of non-empty colour names, and the column holds one of those or NULL. There is no falsy-but-present value for the two operators to disagree about.

The stored id is a canonical Message-ID, and canonicalizeMessageId returns null rather than an empty string, so a representative's id is never falsy. `own` is non-empty for the same reason — the branch is only entered when it is truthy.
The map value is an array, and an array is truthy even when empty. The two operators can differ only on a key that is absent, where both build a new empty array.
Same: an array value, truthy whether or not it has elements.
A row id is a UUID — never the empty string — so the fallback is reachable only when there is no latest row at all, where both operators give ''.
from_addr is NOT NULL and may legitimately be '', but the fallback is also '': when the column is empty both operators produce the empty string, and when there is no row both take the fallback.
Same shape as from_addr: NOT NULL, may be empty, and the fallback is the empty string, so the falsy-but-present case lands on the same value.
Same again — a NOT NULL text column whose fallback is the empty string it might itself hold.
`h.last_date` is MAX(date) over the same thread and `latest` is that thread's newest row, so a `latest.date` of 0 implies `h.last_date` is 0 too. The only falsy date makes both operators produce 0.
The colour names are non-empty strings and the column is otherwise NULL, so there is no falsy-but-present value to distinguish the operators.
to_addr is NOT NULL with '' as its fallback, so an empty column and a missing row both reach collectDisplayNames with the same empty string.
Same: an empty from_addr and an absent row both hand extractName the empty string.
A Map value here is always an array, which is truthy; only an absent key reaches the fallback, and both operators take it.
The cc column is null or a header string, and the fallback is the empty string. A stored '' and a NULL therefore produce the same value under either operator.

The falsy-but-present case is an empty References header, which reaches every consumer through tokenizeReferences — and tokenizeReferences returns [] for '' and for null alike. Neither the threading nor the reply builder can tell the two apart.
Array value or missing key, as above: truthy when present, so the operators agree.

completed_at is set from Date.now() when a task is ticked off, so the only falsy value it could hold is 0 — and the fallback is 0. These rows are selected with `status = 'completed'`, so the column is never NULL here either.
The map's values are objects, which are truthy; only a missing folder key reaches the fallback, where both operators give null.

equivalent.code: return { messageCount: counted.n, latestMessageId: newest?.mid ?? null }
equivalent.reason: `mid` is COALESCE(message_id, id) — a Message-ID or a row UUID, neither of which is empty. The fallback only fires when the thread has no rows.
ai_analysis_at is a timestamp written with the analysis; the only falsy value it could carry is 0, which is also the fallback.
MAX(uid) over a folder's rows: NULL when the folder is empty, otherwise a server UID of 1 or more. A maxUid of 0 and the fallback of 0 are the same number, so the operators cannot be distinguished.
The column starts at 0 and only rises, and the fallback is 0 — the falsy-but-present value and the fallback are the same.
MODSEQ is stored as the decimal string of a 64-bit counter, so the column holds a non-empty string or NULL; setFolderHighestModseq is the only writer and it is called with a value from the server.
server_uid is a POP3 UIDL. pop3-sync only ever writes a UIDL it read from the maildrop listing, and an entry with no UIDL is not a message it can identify — so the empty string is never stored.
The existing row's id is a UUID, never empty, so the fallback is reachable only when there is no existing row.

The only caller that sets this is pop3-sync, which passes a UIDL from the maildrop listing; IMAP callers leave it undefined. An empty UIDL is not an identity and never reaches here, so the falsy-but-present case does not occur.
folders.unread_count is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so the falsy value it can hold is 0 — the same as the fallback.
Same column, same argument: 0 is both the falsy stored value and the fallback, so the sum is unchanged either way.
The search row mapper, reading the same column as the summary mapper: non-empty colour names or NULL, with no falsy-but-present value between them.
Every entry in SEARCH_META_COLUMNS is a non-empty array of column names, and an array is truthy. Only a `field` outside the union reaches the fallback, where both operators take it.

equivalent.code: if ('code' in err) return String((err as { code?: unknown }).code ?? '')
equivalent.reason: The falsy-but-present cases are `code: ''` — where both operators give '' — and a numeric `code: 0`, where `??` gives '0'. Neither is in UNREACHABLE_CODES, and the caller guards with `if (code && ...)`, so '0' and '' both fall through to the message matching and produce the same classification. No thrown object in Node carries a zero errno anyway; the `??` is there to keep the return type a string.

A `message` of '' gives '' under both operators. A numeric `message: 0` gives '0' under `??`, which matches none of the unreachable patterns — the same answer as ''. The classification cannot distinguish them.
The only falsy-but-present subject is the empty string, and the fallback is the empty string, so both operators feed the same value into the prefix stripping.

`first` has already been tested for truthiness on the same line, and a truthy string has length one or more. The length check is a redundant second guard, so `> 0` and `>= 0` are reached only with values they agree on.
Same redundancy: `root &&` has already excluded the empty string, so the length comparison never sees zero.

A reduce picking the newest timestamp. On a tie the two operators choose different *objects* and the same *number*, and only the number is returned — `a.lastSyncAt` and `newest` are equal in exactly the case where they differ.
`status.accounts` is an object or absent, and an object is truthy whether or not it has keys. The two operators can differ only on a falsy-but-present value, which this field cannot hold.
The same field, read a second time in the same module: an object or absent, with no falsy-but-present case between them.

`error` is a non-empty message or null, and the fallback is the empty string. An error of '' — if one could occur — is tested against the same pattern as the fallback, so the two operators give the same answer either way.

The map holds folder display names, which come from an IMAP path's last segment and are never empty — a mailbox with no name cannot be selected or listed. Only a missing folder id reaches the fallback, where both operators take it.
Same field as above: a folder's name is a non-empty path segment, so the fallback is reachable only when there is no folder at all.
unread_count is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so the only falsy value it can hold is 0 — which is also the fallback.

equivalent.code: const [hi, lo] = a > b ? [a, b] : [b, a]
equivalent.reason: Ordering two luminances so the larger is first. The operators differ only when a === b, where `[a, b]` and `[b, a]` hold the same two numbers and the ratio computed from them is 1 either way.

equivalent.code: return lum !== null && contrast(lum, DARK_SURFACE) < MIN_CONTRAST
equivalent.reason: Boundary-only, and the boundary is unreachable. Checked exhaustively: over all 16,777,216 integer RGB values, no colour produces a contrast against DARK_SURFACE of exactly 4.5 — the closest any comes is 7.7e-9 away. A fractional channel is expressible in CSS (`rgb(127.3, 0, 0)`) but would have to land on that ratio exactly, which is a transcendental equality no stylesheet is written to hit.

equivalent.code: return lum !== null && contrast(DARK_TEXT, lum) < MIN_CONTRAST
equivalent.reason: The same exhaustive check against DARK_TEXT: no integer RGB triple gives exactly 4.5, the closest being 1.3e-9 away. Same argument for fractional channels.

A colon at index 0 is a declaration with an empty property name, like `:red`. Skipping it and processing it reach the same place: the property is '', which matches none of `color`, `background` or `background-color`, so the loop moves on either way.

The result is only ever property-accessed (.message/.code/.response/.responseText/.authenticationFailed), and every falsy non-nullish value that `||` would replace with {} — 0, '', false, NaN — yields undefined for all five properties anyway. `?? {}` and `|| {}` are therefore indistinguishable here. The separate `String(err ?? '')` on the next line IS distinguishable and is pinned by test:pure ('a falsy non-nullish thrown value is kept, not discarded').

The array is filtered by `typeof v === 'string' && v.trim().length > 0`, so element [0] is either a non-empty string or undefined — never a falsy string. `??` and `||` can only differ on a falsy non-nullish element, which the filter has already excluded. The filter itself is load-bearing and pinned separately by test:pure ('a blank response does not beat a real one'), which is what stops that guarantee being quietly removed.
